newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan Japan to sell 16 stores to Daiei.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan Japan to sell 16 stores to Daiei.

text.p: Yaohan Japan Corp said on Monday that it had agreed with major supermarket chain operator Daiei Inc to sell 16 of its outlets for 33 billion yen.

The two companies said in separate statements that the 16 outlets, all in central Japan, would be sold to Seifu Kabushiki Kaisha, a chainstore operator owned 89.8 percent by Daiei, in the middle of May.

Yaohan said the sale, part of a broad restructuring programme it announced earlier this month, would make possible the redemption of corporate bonds due in May. The sale would also greatly help to implement other steps included in the restructuring programme, it said.

Daiei said in its statement that it had decided to purchase the 16 outlets at the request of Yaohan. It said the purchase would help strengthen its sales network in central Japan. officials themselves called "excessive" investment both at home and overseas.

In common with other Japanese retail chains, Yaohan, the flagship firm of an international retailing group, was expanding into overseas markets but was more aggressive than others in its push offshore, even moving its group corporate headquarters outside Japan.
Earlier this month, it announced a restructuring programme featuring a reduction of group debt subject to interest payments to 90 billion yen from 164.6 billion yen in the next two years.

Yaohan said at the time that it planned to sell more than 10 stores and offices in the next two years. Stores and offices expected to be sold as part of the restructuring plan had a total book value of 55 billion yen, it said.
Yaohan also said at the time that it would receive financial assistance from Tokai Bank Ltd, Sumitomo Trust and Banking Co Ltd and the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd.
In addition, it said it would cut its group assets to 170 billion yen by the end of March 1999 from 249.4 billion yen at the end of March 1996.

In December, Yaohan said it would close one of its stores in Singapore in June, sell part of its stake in a Malaysian affiliate and relaunch one of its Thai stores as a wholesale facility. It said it would also freeze or postpone plans to open new outlets in Japan.

Also in December, an official of another key company in the Yaohan group said the group would slow its expansion in China, pushing back by one year its plan to have 1,000 stores throughout the Yangtze River delta by the year 2005.
Yaohan Japan also said on Monday that it expected to post parent sales of 85 billion yen in the year starting on April 1, down from estimated 1996/97 sales of 166.00 billion yen.
